tn.quote: Dana displays three contrastive tone levels (L, M, H) as well as a falling (F) contour tone on a single vowel nucleus. Evidence for the tonal contrast is seen in (31). (31) H M L F d̪ ám d̪ ā d̪ à d̪ â ‘thing’ ‘go.SG’ ‘what’ ‘go.PL’ … Tone plays an important role in the verb system. Dana employs tonal alternations on verb roots and stems to mark nominal number of participants as well as verbal number, or pluractionality (cf. Newman 1990). … Most common is the alternation between L and H. The M/H and F/LH alternations are less frequent in the database overall.
tn.cite: Otero, Manuel Alejandro. 2019. A Historical Reconstruction of the Koman Language Family. PhD dissertation, Department of Linguistics, University of Oregon. xxii+734 pp.

tn.note: Three level tones (low, mid, high) plus a falling contour on one vowel; a rising contour is also mentioned; verb roots alternate in tone (mostly L/H) to mark number; no consonant-tone restrictions. tn.quote: Chen exhibits four tones, three of which are level tones and one falling. Phonation plays a role in the tone system: three tones are produced with modal phonation and one with glottalisation. … Open syllables may carry any of the four tones, syllables that end in a nasal may carry tone 1, 2, or 3, and syllables that end in a stop have the least options - they may carry only tone 2 or 3. … tone 1 has a mid to low falling contour. … Tone 4, as indicated in Table 8, is characterised by a high level pitch contour and glottalisation.

5466.idn: Name in the source: Cicipu; family in the source: Kambari subgroup (not Kamuku) of Kainji (Benue-Congo)

tn.quote: Cicipu vowels are found with two contrastive tones: H and L, with contour tones being found on long vowels and diphthongs. … Verb lexemes are inherently toneless, deriving their surface tones from their Tense-Aspect- Mood properties … Falling or rising tones can occur phonetically as a consequence of applying a particular tone pattern to a long vowel, diphthong, or sequence of two vowels. … Note that while LH tones can arise from the overlay of grammatical tone patterns, they are never lexically specified. … Non-automatic downstepped H tones also occur.
tn.cite: McGill, Stuart. 2014. Cicipu. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 44(3): 303-318 (Illustrations of the IPA). doi:10.1017/S002510031400022X

tn.note: Two level tones, H and L; contours only on long vowels or diphthongs, as tone sequences. Nouns have lexical root tone, verbs are toneless and take mood/aspect melodies; non-automatic downstep.

tn.quote: Basically there are two discrete tone levels, high and low, together with a feature of downstep, lowering of the high tone level (3.14). Underlying tones on all final syllables are complex, being a combination of two tones

tn.quote: One of the most intriguing features of Htanaw phonology is the presence of three lexical tones (four according to some authors). On the surface, this looks similar to the Burmese tone system … The phonetic realization of the tones are not identical in the two languages … Tones in Htanaw do not only have lexical function, but they also express grammatical functions. Most prominently, in possessive and oblique contexts, low and mid tones change to high. … Table 2: Influence in phonology … Tones Low-falling, Mid-falling, … High-rising … Gramm. tone L, M → H; POSS, OBL

5470.idn: Name in the source: Ekpeye; family in the source: closely related to Igbo but not mutually intelligible with it; 'must be recognised as a separate language' (neighbours Ogba and Ikwere 'also related to Igbo')

tn.quote: The tone-bearing unitw is the syllable, which is of the pattern V, OV, or rarely N. There are five units of tone, three of level pitch, and two of gliding pitch* The three level tones are termed High, Low and Downstep … "Doivnstep” is used as a label rather than "Mid" since this tone occurs only after a high* After a Low, the contrast between High and Downstep is neutralised* … The two gliding tones both show a fall in pitch, one from High to Low, the other from High to Downstep* … Very few tonal minimal pairs have been found. Thus, lexically tone carries a low functional load

tn.quote: Verb roots in Kifuliiru fall into three classes: High (H), Low (L) and toneless (Ø). The lexical tone (if any) of the verb always appears in stem‑initial position. … Verbal extensions are all toneless with the exception of Passive (PS), Causative (CS), and CS + PS, any of which contributes a single floating H tone. Every Tense/ Aspect/ Mood (TAM) includes one of six melodies: H, L, HL, LH, HH or LL. … Tonal contours in Kifuliiru appear exclusively in the penult … Therefore I posit that tone association is to the syllable, not to the mora.
tn.cite: Van Otterloo, Karen. 2014. Tonal melodies in the Kifuliiru verbal system. Africana Linguistica 20: 385-403. doi:10.3406/aflin.2014.1041
tn.locator: p. 386, sec. 1 'Introduction' (opening paragraphs) and p. 387, sec. 1.2 'Tonal contours'
tn.note: Two tones, H and L (toneless units surface L by default); verb roots are H, L or toneless; each tense adds one of six H/L melodies; HL/LH contours only on the penult; syllable TBU; floating H.

5472.idn: Name in the source: Guébie; family in the source: Kru; 'an Eastern Kru language' (p. 419)

tn.quote: Guébie has four contrastive tone heights labelled 1–4, of which 4 is the highest. All morphemes, with the exception of the definite suffix (Sande 2017), are associated with an underlying tone melody, and surface with that tone melody unless some phonological or grammatical tonal alternation applies. … a super­high tone, tone 5, can also surface. A tone 5 is derived from an underlying high tone, tone 4, plus a grammatical tone raising process. Contrastive underlying tone melodies include levels 1, 2, 3 and 4 and contours 41, 42, 31, 32, 23 and 24.
tn.cite: Sande, Hannah. 2022. Is grammatical tone item-based or process-based? Phonology 39(3): 399-442. Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/S0952675723000106 (first published online 2 October 2023; CC BY 4.0).

evidence_works.note: Jita data are the author's own field notes (Sources, p. 516: 'J'AI UTILISE MES PROPRES NOTES... POUR LES LANGUES SUIVANTES:... - jita, ruri (groupe VI)'; the procedure is stated only generically for the whole set of languages: from a word list and a few verb forms collected in one afternoon up to tens of hours of recording), plus Downing 1988, 'Tonology of noun-modifier phrases in Jita', a paper presented at the 19th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, Boston, listed under Jita in the bibliography (Groupe VI (Suguti), p. 520). Jita is marked '++' (well described) in Table 1 (E 25, groupe VI Suguti, p. 72). Tone-system detail consistent with the entry: three tone patterns on disyllabic nominal stems (BB, BH, HB), p. 412; Meeussen's rule present; displaced association (a H shifts to the following syllable) except that a H on the penultimate or final before absolute pause escapes the shift, pp. 132-133, 485, 502; nominals ending in two unmarked syllables receive a final mark phrase-internally, pp. 133, 340-341. The thesis labels the system 'langue accentuelle à mélodie H' (p. 502) and 'le jita (analysable, lui aussi, comme langue à accent)' (p. 132): this is the author's representational framework (privative marked syllables plus a H melody) applied to almost every language in the survey, not a claim that Jita lacks lexical tone, and does not bear on tone_cls.

5481.idn: Name in the source: kanyok; the statement concerns a variety of this language (kanyôk de l'ouest (bwiin kanyôk, Western Kanyok))

tn.quote: L'absence d'un signe sur une voyelle ou sur des voyelles successives Indique qu'el le(s) porte(nt) un ton haut. L'accent grave marque un ton bas. L'accent circonflexe ou la séquence "sans signe" suîvied'un accent grave symbolise un ton descendant. Le trait vertical indique l'abaissement du ton haut par rapport au ton haut immédiatement précédent. L'accent grave flottant, enfin, marque un ton descendant postérieur et il est en distribution complémentaire avec le ton haut abaissé.
tn.translation: The absence of a sign on a vowel or on successive vowels indicates that it/they bear a high tone. The grave accent marks a low tone. The circumflex, or the sequence 'no sign' followed by a grave accent, symbolises a falling tone. The vertical stroke indicates the lowering of the high tone relative to the immediately preceding high tone. The floating grave accent, finally, marks a posterior falling tone and is in complementary distribution with the lowered high tone.
tn.cite: Stappers, Leo, L. Mulaji & T. Kalela. 1980. Textes kanyok. Africana Linguistica 8 (Annales MRAC 101): 199-226.
tn.locator: Introduction, 'Les tons', p. 202
tn.note: Western Kanyok texts mark high, low and falling tones on every vowel, plus a lowered (downstepped) high after a high and a floating final falling tone in complementary distribution with it.

Manakala bagi nada tinggi / / di tempat-tempat lain. … Sementara bagi vokal panjang, bunyi aspirasi dan bernada tidak akan ditemui dalam DML. Mudahnya, ciri ini tiada pada DML. … Begitu juga bagi vokal panjang dan nada, kedua-duanya hadir pada bahasa Thai tetapi tidak pada DSL dan DST. Ini bermakna masyarakat Satun banyak meminjam leksikal dari Thai. Yang jelasnya, leksikal ini dipinjam bersama ciri fonologinya.
tn.translation: According to Court (in Gandour 1979), the tone that enters Malay, especially DST [Thai Satun dialect], is mostly the rising-falling tone / ˆ/, especially on open final syllables, and the high tone / ´/ elsewhere. … As for long vowels, aspirated sounds and toned sounds, they will not be found in DML [Langkawi Malay dialect]. Simply, these features are absent in DML. … Likewise for long vowels and tone: both are present in Thai but not in DSL and DST. This means the Satun community borrows much lexicon from Thai. Clearly, this lexicon is borrowed together with its phonological features.

tn.quote: Le chapitre 4 quant à lui nous a présenté les tons qui meublent le kwó. Ainsi, sur le plan phonétique, nous constatons que la langue possède 5 tons dont 3 tons ponctuels et 2 tons modulés. Sur le plan phonologique cependant, l‟étude révèle 2 tons à savoir le ton haut et le ton bas. Le ton moyen et les tons modulés sont issus des processus phonologiques et ne s‟inscrivent par conséquent pas dans le tableau tonémique du kwó. Pour finir, nous avons vu que, le kwó a 3 fonctions tonales à savoir: une fonction distinctive, une fonction grammaticale, une fonction lexicale.
tn.translation: Chapter 4 presented the tones found in Kwó. On the phonetic level we find that the language has 5 tones, 3 level tones and 2 contour tones. On the phonological level, however, the study reveals 2 tones, namely the high tone and the low tone. The mid tone and the contour tones result from phonological processes and therefore do not belong to the tonemic chart of Kwó. Finally, we saw that Kwó has 3 tonal functions: a distinctive, a grammatical and a lexical function.
tn.cite: Lekebai, Oscar. 2025. Phonologie du Kwó. Mémoire de Master, Université de Yaoundé I (Faculté des Arts, Lettres et Sciences Humaines; dir. Joseph Mbongue). 134 pp. hdl:20.500.12177/13789 (DICAMES).

tn.quote: 3.3 Tones Jili has three level tones, as the following minimal triplets show; Form Gloss Form Gloss bɛ́ to come ká ‘that he’ bɛ question particle ka to guard bɛ̀ to choose kà to exceed There are also numerous complex glide tones. These symbolised as follows; Rising Low-High hachek over the syllable ˇ Low-Mid Mid-High ∆ Falling High-Low circumflex over the syllable ˆ High-Mid … Mid-Low ƒ … Tones on pronouns change according to the TAM features of the clause in which they occur.
tn.cite: Blench, Roger. 2006. A Dictionary of the Jili (Migili) Language of Central Nigeria [title page: Towards a dictionary of the Jili (Migili) language of Central Nigeria; draft circulated for comment, printout 6 January 2015]. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation / Mallam Dendo. 33 pp. ms., rogerblench.info.
tn.locator: §3.3 Tones, pp. 3-4, and §4.2 Pronouns, p. 4
tn.note: Three level tones, high, mid and low, shown by minimal triplets; six glide tones (LH, LM, MH, HL, HM, ML) written as combinations of levels; pronoun tones change with tense/aspect; nothing on stress.

5488.cfw: Known only second-hand: Blench 2006 reports the tone system after another work; the primary description was not read.

tn.quote: Lugbarati is tonal with three level tones: Low, Mid, and High and a Rising contour tone while some syllables have a HM contour tone. Tone has a very heavy functional load, both in the lexicon and in the grammar. … L ti has three level tones, Low, Mid, High, and, much rarer, a rising contour tone, LH or a falling contour tone HL. It is not yet completely clear what is causing these. This needs further research. There are also syllables with a HM contour. These sound a lot longer and are probably two vowels, the first with a H tone, the second with a M tone.

tn.note: Three level tones (Low, Mid, High) with heavy lexical and grammatical load; much rarer rising LH and falling HL contours; a floating High marks 3rd plural verbs (L becomes LH, M becomes H).
